newsitem.title: USA: RJR Nabisco cuts Q2 EPS view, yr EPS intact.
newsitem.headline: RJR Nabisco cuts Q2 EPS view, yr EPS intact.

text.p: RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp told analysts on Tuesday that while the company is still on track for full-year, per-share net income of $2.99, the concensus estimate of $0.74 for the second quarter is too high.
Hunt Whitacre, director of investor relations, said second-quarter net income per share would be closer to $0.71.
Whitacre's comments came during a conference call that was closed to the media. One analyst who was on the call told Reuters of the revision, which was confirmed by the company.

RJR Nabisco led analysts lower for second-quarter estimates, after meeting first-quarter estimates squarely, because of some operational difficulties -- now corrected -- that would still be showing effects in the near term.

The problems, which occurred during the first quarter, chipped away part of the period's bottom line. They included a reorganization of the domestic-biscuit sales force at the company's Nabisco Holdings Corp subsidiary, and import disruptions in the former Soviet Union, the spokesperson said.

"As a rapidly growing business, we can experience volatility quarter to quarter, but the underlying trends remain very favorable for 1997 and beyond," Chairman and Chief Executive Steven Goldstone said in a statement accompanying the first-quarter results.

RJR Nabisco reported first-quarter net income of $213 million, or $0.62 per share, on net sales of $3.78 billion. In the first quarter of 1996, net income totaled $198 million, or $0.57 per share, on net sales of $3.89 billion
"Export disruption in the former Soviet Union is the primary cause of the slippage in the quarter," the company said.

It said uncertainty regarding taxation policies in the region forced importers to delay purchases in the quarter, but that import order flow began to return to normal late in the quarter and that tax issues have been clarified.
Overall consumption trends in the former Soviet Union remain strong, the company said.
